scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-Sidorenkos-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 161 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0c0d7b5eb1ed43c0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let H be the incidence graph of the 22 triples on 13 points in Table 1. This bipartite graph has 35 vertices and 66 edges. There is a finite simple undirected graph G with at least one edge such that t(H, G) < p(G)66 .
